source: shared working tree with only the listed Knowledge and new Core test changes for this bridge; no Git commit or provider call by this qualification
scope: trusted-local, caller-observed opaque native Run artifact metadata and desired KRAIL procedure candidate; no provider attestation, semantic correctness, or human procedure approval

tests.dependency_boundary: Core .venv supplies test dependencies; appended existing conda site-packages supplies optional DuckDB 1.5.0. No environment was mutated.
Core bridge test explicitly locates sibling Knowledge rail-py; it is not a Core release dependency.

public_boundary_evidence: real Core public worker start, two result publications, and completion APIs publish UTF-8 native text through deterministic fixture worker credentials
authenticated loopback Core Run and final-lease agent-result review select the final artifact, not the earlier draft
KRAIL records the exact returned artifact-byte digest, reopens its durable metadata, and creates a desired procedure revision without inherited test, review, or activation
a separately configured Project adapter cannot read the artifact directly, even with the same human bearer
protected reviewed-memory withdrawal between Core artifact-content response and the final re-identification denies in-call and later KRAIL reads
Project offboarding denies a later evidence read
a real redirect target receives no bearer and encoded metadata is refused
limits: No real Codex or Claude provider turn was made in these tests; worker output is deterministic fixture text.
Core native worker results currently require UTF-8 and at most 512000 bytes; KRAIL treats the returned representation as opaque and bounds reads at 1048576 bytes.
The result has application/octet-stream on the Core content endpoint; no provider media type or provider binary identity is attested.
Exact input refs and installation authority are trusted-local caller declarations; a current authorizer must check those refs independently.
The Core review route used by this adapter is available for personal SQLite composition, not current hosted PostgreSQL.
Core reads and the KRAIL metadata write are separate transactions; revocation during that gap may leave inert retained metadata, but current re-read denies release.

retained_actual_provider_qualification.result: A previously completed actual Codex native result was reread through Core HTTP after personal runtime restart; the exact final artifact was observed, saved and reopened in a separate private KRAIL JSON store, and cited by an inert desired procedure candidate with no review, test evidence, or activation.
retained_actual_provider_qualification.limits: This verifies retained-result compatibility and current human access for one Run. It does not attest the provider binary/model, certify result correctness, exercise production input grants, or approve/activate the candidate. Private Run IDs, bearer, artifact bytes, and content are omitted.
retained_actual_provider_qualification.parent_verification: Parent inspected the private retained observation and confirmed its exact Run, artifact ID and SHA-256 match the earlier packaged native-result receipt. The observation contains no body or bearer.
